answer:
**Supported syntax:** only `*` and `?`, plus a trailing `/` that is stripped.

- The doc comment says the matcher "supports * and ? and trailing /" (src/filter.zig:49).
- The code strips a trailing `/` (src/filter.zig:52-54). `?` matches any single character (src/filter.zig:61), and `*` matches any run of characters (src/filter.zig:64-67, 77-79).
- Tests cover `*.zig`, `test_*.zig`, `target/`, and `file?.log` (src/filter.zig:322-327).

**Is `[abc]` a character class?** No. The matcher has no `[` handling. Any character other than `?` or `*` is compared literally (`p[p_idx] == name[n_idx]`, src/filter.zig:61). So `[abc]` matches only the literal text `[abc]`.

**Caveat:** the context shows `matchPattern` applied to excluded and included patterns (src/filter.zig:286, 309) and in `preApplies` (src/main.zig:790). It doesn't show how `--exclude`/`--include` flags are parsed, so I can't confirm the CLI doesn't preprocess them before they reach the matcher. README and GUIA hits for this topic are absent.
